title: Scaling Orchestrator Safety Profile & Metric Targets
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose: Define a production-ready safety profile, metric targets, and algorithmic design for the Dedicated capacity scaling orchestrator so that tenant throughput guarantees and latency SLOs are met while controlling cost and avoiding unsafe surge behavior.

Scope:
- Metric definitions (targets and windows) for per-tenant and fleet-level scaling decisions.
- Core scaling algorithm (control loops, step rules, warm pool interaction).
- Safety limits and hard fail-safes (surge caps, per-tenant max nodes, cooldowns).
- Fallback behaviors (model variant routing, degraded-mode limits).
- Observability and alerting for anomalous scaling decisions.

Non-goals: deep GPU scheduler changes, billing integration, long-term ML-based autoscaler (future work).

Background: Current Dedicated autoscaling is reactive to simple throughput thresholds and has produced oscillation during bursty traffic, occasionally breaching tenant throughput SLAs or provisioning more capacity than expected during noisy spikes. We need a more deterministic orchestrator that reasons about short-term burst tolerance, steady-state throughput targets, and explicit economic safety constraints.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Scaling decisions are computed from a well-documented set of metrics (per-tenant tokens/sec, p95 latency, GPU_utilization) and use consistent windows (10s, 60s, 5m) explained in the spec.
A2: Implemented algorithm includes an explicit surge budget and per-tenant max-capacity cap; unit tests validate caps under synthetic bursts.
A3: New orchestrator exposes decision logs (reason + contributing metrics) to the Console for audit and debugging.
A4: No user-facing throughput regression vs current baseline in 95% of integration runs; when regressions occur, automatic safe rollback triggers.
A5: Dashboards and alerts for scaling anomalies (unexpected scale-ups, oscillation, queue length growth) are created and linked to runbook.
A6: Gradual rollout plan documented with canary gates and kill-switch that returns traffic to previous autoscaler in <2m.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Metric selection: combine short window (10s) tokens/sec for burst detection with medium window (60s) for sustained demand and long window (5m) for trend smoothing -- this balances sensitivity and stability.
Control algorithm: PI controller with rate-limited step changes and a per-tenant surge budget chosen over a pure ML predictor to keep behavior interpretable and debuggable.
Warm pool handling: prefer retaining a small warm pool for high-SLA tenants; trade-off increases cost but reduces cold-start latency spikes.
Safety vs. cost: enforce a fleet-level surge cap (default 30% above committed capacity) to bound cost; enterprises can request higher caps via Dedicated contract.
KV cache state: conservative scaling (prefer step-up then gradual demotion) to avoid cache churn; aggressive horizontal scaling risks cold-KV penalty and increased latency.
Fallbacks: prefer routing to a cheaper model variant if latency SLOs cannot be met within safety caps rather than unlimited scaling.
algorithm_spec_summary: Inputs: per-tenant tokens/sec (10s/60s/5m), p95 latency (60s), queue length, GPU_utilization per node, model_variant_compatibility flags.
Decision cadence: 10s evaluation loop, but apply scale actions only if conditions persist for configured stability windows (default 30s for scale-up, 300s for scale-down).
Controller: PI controller tuned with conservative gains (Kp, Ki) per tenant class (prod-high, prod-low, dev).
Step policy: limit single-step scale-up to max 20% of current pool or X nodes (whichever smaller) and priority can incrementally use surge budget up to fleet limit.
Cooldowns: post-scale-up cooldown 60s before next increase for same tenant; post-scale-down cooldown 300s to avoid oscillation.
Warm pool rules: maintain a minimum of N warm nodes for tenants with SLA flag; warm nodes count deducted from surge budget calculations.
Safety checks: before committing scale action validate remaining available GPU capacity, cloud quota, and per-tenant hard cap. If any check fails, trigger fallback routing and raise ticket.
safety_limits_and_fail_safes: Per-tenant hard cap: default 50 nodes unless overridden by enterprise config.
Fleet surge cap: default 30% above committed capacity; can be raised with approval (audit trail required).
Per-evaluation node limit: max nodes creatable in a single evaluation is 10 to avoid sudden fleet churn.
Cost gate: cumulative projected cost delta for action must be < configured monthly threshold or action is rejected (for non-enterprise customers).
Manual kill-switch: operations can immediately pause all new scale-ups and let scheduled downs proceed; accessible from Console with audit log.
Auto-rollback: when p95 latency increases >2x baseline after a scale action within 5 minutes, revert the action and mark the decision for postmortem.
observability_and_alerting: Decision logging: structured decision events stored in Events DB with fields: timestamp, tenant, reason_scores (tokens/sec, p95, util), proposed_action, final_action, applied_nodes, trace_id.
Dashboards: per-tenant scaling timeline, surge budget utilization, and oscillation detector chart (scale actions per 15m).
Alerts: scaling-oscillation (>=5 actions in 10m), surge-budget-exhausted, scale-failure (node provisioning error >2 attempts), p95-regression-after-scale.
Runbook: link to runbook and playbook for investigating scaling anomalies and reverting changes.
Synthetic tests: scheduled burst tests against canary tenants to surface regressions before full rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): unit + integration tests against simulator (pass criteria: no oscillation in 90% synthetic traces).
Phase 1 (canary): enable orchestrator for 2% of tenants (non-prod and low-risk prod); monitor surge budget and p95 for 48h.
Phase 2 (staged expansion): incrementally expand to 25% of tenants over 1 week with automated health gates (p95, queue length, cost deltas).
Phase 3 (full): roll to all Dedicated tenants with opt-out option for enterprise customers needing custom caps.
Kill switch: immediate revert to legacy autoscaler via Console toggle; target mean time to revert <120s.
qa_and_test_plan: Simulator tests: run 1000 synthetic traffic traces including heavy-tail bursts, steady ramps, and multi-tenant interference scenarios.
Chaos tests: simulate node provisioning failures, slow starts (cold KV), and API throttles during canary window.
Performance: validate 95th latency and throughput for representative apps (chat generation, embeddings) against baseline clusters.
Integration: end-to-end test with Console decision logs surfaced and confirmed in dashboard.
